data.title: Anthropic and SpaceX prove Nasdaq is crushing the IPO game
data.description:
The trajectory for the Anthropic (ANT) IPO is still up for discussion, but there is one clear winner that has been above the debate. The Nasdaq (NDAQ) has walked away from the notable debut with a swagger after snatching the biggest listing of all time. Less than six months ago, the stock exchange scored another record IPO, wooing SpaceX (SPCX) to its market.

Bigger picture: It's been a bumper year for the Nasdaq (NDAQ), which has outpaced its main rival by a 10x spread. According to Dealogic, there have been 64 Nasdaq IPOs this year that have raised $201.8B, compared to the $20.8B total raised from 42 IPOs on the New York Stock Exchange. Shareholders have been happy with the performance, with Nasdaq (NDAQ) shares climbing 21% over the past year, and 92% over the last three years, nearly double the returns of NYSE-parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). 

"Anthropic's IPO is a very proud moment for us," Nasdaq (NDAQ) CEO Adena Friedman told Reuters. "We've been engaging with the Anthropic team for a very long time. Separate from the entire listing experience, we've been a client to them, as we are to the AI ecosystem, and so we also have gotten to know them in that context as well."

What's the difference? Besides the emphasis on courtship, especially to Silicon Valley and high-growth disruptors, the Nasdaq's (NDAQ) ecosystem provides some structural advantages. Those include significantly lower listing fees, more flexible entry requirements, and generally faster IPO processing. A Nasdaq (NDAQ) listing also offers access to popular benchmarks like the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), and the exchange has even loosened its rules to fast-track names like SpaceX (SPCX) to boost liquidity and broaden the overall shareholder base.

data.title: VisionWave shares jump ~24% on deal for critical minerals intelligence platform
data.description:
• VisionWave Holdings (VWAV) Friday reported the acquisition of the Critical Minerals Intelligence Platform (CMIP), sending shares up ~24% in early trading. VisionWave intends to pursue near-term revenue opportunities through subscription-based intelligence services, compliance documentation, and transaction-related services
  • The agreement with Litial Ltd was signed on November 18, 2026, and the acquisition has not yet closed, the company said.
  • If completed, the acquisition would mark VisionWave's entry into the defense-industrial supply chain intelligence market and is intended to establish a new commercial technology offering with the potential to generate recurring revenue through subscriptions, compliance-related services, and transaction-based fees.
  • The platform initially focuses on tungsten and antimony, two materials of strategic importance to defense, aerospace, and advanced manufacturing. VisionWave also sees the potential to extend the platform to other critical minerals, specialized industrial materials, and defense-related components.

data.title: JBS establishes a new multiprotein platform in Oman
data.description:
JBS N.V. (JBS) announced it established a new multiprotein production platform in Oman that covers beef, poultry, and lamb.

The company holds an 80% stake in a newly established food holding entity that consolidates two production assets in Oman, while Oman Food Capital holds the remaining 20% stake. Oman Food Capital is the food and agribusiness investment arm of the Oman Investment Authority. 

The joint venture is expected to contribute to strengthening food security in Oman, in line with the Sultanate’s Vision 2040, while positioning the country as a strategic platform for the production of halal food products for export to multiple markets. The initiative is designed to serve the global halal market, which currently encompasses an estimated 2B consumers worldwide. With the investments, the operation is expected to reach an estimated static industrial production capacity of approximately 300K tons per year. That capacity corresponds to the daily processing of approximately 1K head of cattle, 5K lambs, and 600K chickens.

On a broader scale, JBS (JBS) noted that the initiative reinforces its strategy of diversification by geography and protein and proximity to key consumer markets.

Shares of JBS (JBS) are down 9.6% over the last month. The dividend yield for new buyers of the stock is 8.4%.

data.title: Hunger Games opening vs. GTA 6? The odds still favor a big box office weekend
data.description:
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping hits theaters on November 20. Adapted from Suzanne Collins’s bestselling novel and directed by franchise veteran Francis Lawrence, the prequel shifts the spotlight to a sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy, played by Joseph Zada. The cast includes Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, and Glenn Close.

Advance ticket sales are reported to be strong. Box office analysts project a debut between $100M and $125M for the 6th Hunger Games film across roughly 3.9K theaters. While Lionsgate (LION) is publicly maintaining a more conservative estimate around $85M, exhibitors and box office trackers expect strong presales and fan demand to push it comfortably into nine-figure territory. With the lucrative Thanksgiving holiday around the corner, the film is seen as well-positioned for a strong multi-week run. The film appears likely to cruise past its production cost of $150M.

While there has been some speculation that the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 is a major attention and spending event that could create some headwinds for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, most box office watchers expect the movie's core fanbase to still carry it to a strong opening.

A strong box office opening could impact theater-related stocks, including AMC Entertainment (AMC), Cinemark Holdings (CNK), IMAX (IMAX), National CineMedia (NCMI), and Reading International (RDI).

data.title: Fed regional bank staff to get smaller pay hikes in 2027 - report
data.description:
The Federal Reserve’s board approved a smaller budget for pay hikes at the central bank's 12 regional banks, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The funds approved for pay raises would result in minimum annual hikes of 1% across the system in 2027, Fed regional bank officials told employees. That's down from 3% this year.

Board staff in Washington, who received 1% raises this year, will get similar hikes next year.

The Fed didn't provide a reason for the budget changes. In one instance, employees were told that the Fed board's decision didn't reflect employee performance.

Many civilian federal workers received a 1% raise this year and a pay freeze is expected next year, WSJ reported.

data.title: SK Hynix to become Kioxia's largest shareholder after bond conversion
data.description:
SK Hynix (SKHY) will become the largest shareholder in Japanese chipmaker Kioxia Holdings (KXIAY) after converting bonds held through an investment vehicle into shares in December.

The South Korean chipmaker said it would convert the bonds into 129,000 common shares and purchase an additional 1,001 shares in the investment vehicle from Bain Capital. The transaction will give SK Hynix an indirect stake of about 14.1% in Kioxia.

SK Hynix said it has no immediate plans to buy or sell more Kioxia shares and will continue to have limited involvement in the Japanese company's management.

SK Hynix invested a total of 395B yen ($2.48B) in 2018 in a Bain Capital-led consortium that acquired Toshiba Memory, which was later renamed Kioxia.

A Bain-managed investment vehicle completed the sale of all its Kioxia shares in June, following the company's listing on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in December 2024.

data.title: Q3 earnings season winds down: 10 consumer discretionary stocks that beat estimates
data.description:
As the third-quarter earnings season draws to a close, a group of consumer discretionary companies has delivered earnings-per-share results that exceeded Wall Street expectations, offering pockets of resilience across an otherwise mixed consumer spending environment.

A screen of stocks based on Seeking Alpha's quantitative metrics identifies Hilton Grand Vacations Inc. (HGV) as the biggest earnings surprise, with an EPS Surprise of $2.92. RH (RH) follows with $2.24, while Abercrombie & Fitch Co. (ANF) and AutoZone, Inc. (AZO) each recorded surprises of $2.21.

The results span businesses ranging from travel and home furnishings to apparel and automotive retail, highlighting how earnings strength has varied across different consumer-facing industries.

Cavco Industries, Inc. (CVCO) ranks fifth with an EPS Surprise of $1.75, followed by American Public Education, Inc. (APEI) at $1.66. Murphy USA Inc. (MUSA) comes next with $1.09, while Hasbro, Inc. (HAS) posted a surprise of $1.05.

Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. (CBRL) and Burlington Stores, Inc. (BURL) round out the top 10, with surprises of $0.81 and $0.77, respectively. Hilton Grand Vacations' lead is notable, with its $2.92 reading exceeding the next-highest surprise by $0.68. 

The list also covers a broad range of business models, including homebuilding, education services, leisure products and restaurants. Market capitalizations range from $774.19 million for American Public Education to $53.25 billion for AutoZone, reflecting the diversity of companies included in the screen.

The earnings results come as U.S. retailers enter the crucial holiday shopping period, with consumer spending patterns and price sensitivity likely to remain important considerations. According to the National Retail Federation's latest holiday forecast, November and December retail sales are expected to increase between 3.7% and 4.2% in 2026, reaching between $1.01 trillion and $1.02 trillion.

However, the spending outlook remains uneven, as consumers continue to balance discretionary purchases against higher living costs. 

EPS Surprise measures the dollar difference between a company's reported earnings per share and the consensus analyst estimate. A positive figure indicates that actual earnings exceeded Wall Street expectations, while a negative reading means results fell short.
